title: Per-job command timeout override is capped at 300s while the app and presets allow 3600s — long-running script jobs can't be tuned upward
existing_state: JobEditorValidator.MaxCommandTimeoutOverrideSeconds is 300 (Utilities/JobEditorValidator.cs:13) and the Advanced-tab NumericUpDown is bound to that maximum (JobEditorDialog.cs:1249-1250), but everywhere else in the app a command timeout may be up to 3600s (InputValidator.IsValidTimeout, Utilities/InputValidator.cs:95-98). Worse, when the user first checks 'Override command timeout', the control is seeded with the inherited app/preset timeout passed through ClampNumericValue (JobEditorDialog.cs:1501-1507) — so a job targeting a preset with a 20-minute timeout silently shows 300, and the override can only ever shorten, never extend, beyond 5 minutes. Long-running YAML script jobs (config backups, firmware staging) are a core use case for the scheduler, and this is exactly where a per-job timeout bump is wanted.
recommendation: Raise MaxCommandTimeoutOverrideSeconds to 3600 to match InputValidator.IsValidTimeout (one constant in Utilities/JobEditorValidator.cs:13; the NumericUpDown maximum and the validation message at JobEditorValidator.cs:199 follow automatically). Update the corresponding bound in JobEditorValidationTests if asserted. Optionally, when the seeded inherited value would have been clamped, surface it in the guidance label ('Inherited: preset X timeout (1200 sec)') instead of silently snapping the spinner.
user_benefit: Scheduled jobs running long scripts can finally be given the timeout they need per job instead of forcing a global or per-preset change; removes a silent surprise where the editor shows 300 for a 1200-second inherited timeout.

evidence.note: App-wide timeout validity allows up to 3600s
Spinner bound to the 300 cap; inherited value silently clamped on first check via ClampNumericValue
